text.p: Gas pipeline company Transportadora de Gas del Sur (TGS) criticized a ruling by Argentine gas regulator Enargas Friday cutting its tariffs, saying the decision breached the gas privatization framework.

Enargas said Friday it was cutting TGS's tariffs by 6.5 percent for five years from January 1998, after "taking into account efficiency improvements that the regulator believes the license holders can attain in the next five years."
But TGS said it thought the move was unfair.

"We believe that the methodology applied in arriving at the efficiency factor is inconsistent with the letter and spirit of the regulatory framework promoted by the Argentine governent in the privatization of Gas del Estado. Obviously, we are assessing our options in light of the Enargas resolution," TGS Chief Executive Officer K.George Wasaff said in a news release.
Enargas said this is the first tariff revision since the privatization of state-owned Gas del Estado which divided the industry up into eight distribution companies and two transport companies.
The regulator also cut tariffs for other gas transport and distribution companies.

TGS is owned 70 percent by Compania de Inversiones de Energia SA (CIESA). CIESA is owned 50 percent by Argentina's Perez Companc and a Perez Companc subsidiary, 33.3 percent by Enron Pipeline Co Argentina, and 16.7 percent by Enron Argentina CIESA Holding.
